cards.explanation: The answer is his ancestor King David. The text says Josiah "…walked in all the ways of his father David…" (2 Kings 22:2). David is the king Israel anointed at Hebron (2 Samuel 5:3). So the man on the throne at eight years old is following a path that was already marked out for him.

The answer is repairing the damaged temple. Verse 5 says the workmen are "…repairing the damages to the house of the LORD…" and verse 6 says the money buys what they need "…to repair the temple." Carpenters, builders and masons are fixing what's already there, friends. It's a patch job, and somebody's definitely going home with sawdust in their sandals.

The answer is timber. Verse 6 says the money is "…to buy timber and dressed stone to repair the temple." That's for the carpenters, builders and masons. Nobody ever fixed a wall with good intentions alone, friends.

The word is integrity. King Josiah says they "…need not account for the money put into their hands, since they work with integrity." (2 Kings 22:7). That's a real compliment from the king himself. Being trusted like that is worth more than a whole tray of warm cookies.

The answer is the Book of the Law. Hilkiah says, "I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD!" (2 Kings 22:8). He hands it to Shaphan, who reads it. It's like finding your keys in the pocket of the coat you wore yesterday, friends, except this time it's the Book of the Law.

The answer is False. Shaphan starts with the money in verse 9: "Your servants have paid out the money that was found in the temple and have put it into the hands of the workers and supervisors of the house of the LORD." Only then, in verse 10, does he say, "Hilkiah the priest has given me a book." He finishes the errand he was sent on, friends, and then the book comes up.

The answer is True. Verse 11 says, "When the king heard the words of the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes…" The words were just read out loud, and the king reacts right then. I think this is a heavy moment, friends, and the text lets it be heavy.

The answer is go and ask the LORD about it. The king commands them, "Go and inquire of the LORD for me, for the people, and for all Judah concerning the words in this book that has been found." (2 Kings 22:13). He sends them to ask the LORD, friends. And he wants the answer for himself, the people and all Judah.

The answer is True. Josiah says, "…great is the wrath of the LORD that burns against us because our fathers have not obeyed the words of this book…" (2 Kings 22:13). He ties it to the book that was just read to him. Those are heavy words, friends, and the king says them plainly.

The answer is Huldah the prophetess. Verse 14 says the men "…went and spoke to Huldah the prophetess…" She lived in Jerusalem, and she's the one who gives them the LORD's message (2 Kings 22:15). And hear this, friends: the king's own men come to her door.

The answer is True. Huldah says the LORD declares, "I am about to bring calamity on this place and on its people, according to all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read…" (2 Kings 22:16). It lines up with the book the king heard. That's a hard message, friends, and she delivers it as it was given.

The answer is that they forsook Him for other gods. The LORD says, "…they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands." (2 Kings 22:17). That's the reason He gives, and it's the only one in the verse. It's a serious word, friends, and the text lets it stand.

The word is tender. The LORD says, "…because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before the LORD when you heard what I spoke against this place and against its people…" (2 Kings 22:19). A tender heart is a soft one, not a hard one, friends. And the LORD points it out Himself.

The word is peace. The LORD says, "Therefore I will indeed gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace." (2 Kings 22:20). Peace is the word He uses for Josiah. That's a kind promise, friends, for a king who just heard hard news.

The answer is False. The LORD says to Josiah, "Your eyes will not see all the calamity that I will bring on this place." (2 Kings 22:20). That promise comes with the one about being gathered to his grave in peace. The LORD says it plainly, friends, and the king gets to hear it.
